title: Fix the Global Counter Update
description: The program should increment a global counter each time a function is called. Fix the bug.
buggyCode:
counter = 0

def increment():
    counter = counter + 1

increment()
print(counter)
expectedBehavior: The program should print 1 after calling increment() once.
actualProblem: Assigning to counter inside the function makes Python treat it as a new local variable for the whole function body, so reading counter on the right-hand side before it's locally assigned raises an UnboundLocalError.
correctedCode:
counter = 0

def increment():
    global counter
    counter = counter + 1

increment()
print(counter)
explanation: To modify a module-level variable from inside a function, the function must declare it with the global keyword. Without it, any assignment to that name creates a separate local variable instead.
